title: Roasted Garlic Primavera Linguine
dek: Light, garlicky linguine loaded with zucchini, mushrooms, peppers, tomatoes, and herbs instead of a heavy cream sauce.
image_alt: Vegetable linguine with roasted garlic and herbs

instructions.name: Cook pasta
instructions.text: Boil linguine until al dente and reserve 1 1/2 cups pasta water.

instructions.name: Brown mushrooms
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wide skillet. Brown mushrooms without stirring constantly.

instructions.name: Cook vegetables
instructions.text: Add remaining oil, zucchini, pepper, and tomatoes. Cook until just tender.

instructions.name: Build the sauce
instructions.text: Stir in roasted garlic, red pepper flakes, 3/4 cup pasta water, lemon zest, and Parmesan.

instructions.name: Toss
instructions.text: Add linguine and toss vigorously. Finish with lemon juice, herbs, black pepper, and more pasta water as needed.

why_it_works: Roasted garlic gives the sauce body and sweetness without cream.
Vegetables are cooked in stages so mushrooms brown while zucchini stays firm.
Pasta water and Parmesan make a light sauce that still clings.
swaps: Make it vegan with nutritional yeast and extra olive oil.
Add grilled chicken for extra protein.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet with a splash of water.
notes: Salt the pasta water well because the sauce is intentionally light.
Do not crowd mushrooms if you want browning.

faqs.a: Yes, but thaw and dry them first to avoid a watery sauce.
Yes. Use nutritional yeast or a dairy-free Parmesan.
Linguine, spaghetti, penne, or farfalle all work.

title: Teriyaki Chicken & Egg Rice Bowls
dek: Sticky teriyaki chicken over rice with soft egg, greens, sesame, and scallions.
image_alt: Teriyaki chicken rice bowl with egg sesame and greens
ingredients: 2 tbsp mirin or 1 tbsp honey plus 1 tbsp rice vinegar

instructions.name: Sear the chicken
instructions.text: Cook chicken thighs in oil over medium-high until browned and cooked through. Transfer and slice.

instructions.name: Mix the sauce
instructions.text: Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, mirin, rice vinegar, ginger, garlic, cornstarch, and 1/3 cup water.

instructions.name: Glaze
instructions.text: Pour sauce into the skillet and simmer until glossy. Return sliced chicken and toss.

instructions.name: Cook the eggs
instructions.text: Fry or soft-boil eggs to your preferred doneness. Wilt spinach briefly in the warm skillet.

instructions.name: Build
instructions.text: Serve rice with chicken, spinach, egg, scallions, sesame seeds, and nori.

why_it_works: Chicken thighs stay juicy under a sticky glaze.
Cornstarch thickens the sauce fast without reducing it into saltiness.
Egg yolk adds richness so the bowl needs less sauce.
swaps: Use brown rice or cauliflower rice.
storage: Refrigerate chicken and rice up to 4 days. Cook eggs fresh when possible.
notes: Low-sodium soy sauce keeps the finished glaze balanced.
Let the sauce bubble for at least 30 seconds to cook the cornstarch.

faqs.q: Can I use bottled teriyaki sauce?
faqs.a: Yes, but this quick homemade sauce gives you better control over sweetness.
Yes. Chicken and rice meal-prep very well.
Yes. It is savory-sweet and not spicy.

title: Orange-Ginger Chicken Rice Bowls
dek: Bright orange-glazed chicken with peppers and onion over rice—sticky, savory, and faster than delivery.
image_alt: Orange glazed chicken rice bowl with peppers and onion
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water

instructions.name: Coat chicken
instructions.text: Toss chicken with 2 tablespoons cornstarch and a pinch of salt.

instructions.name: Brown
instructions.text: Heat oil in a large skillet and cook chicken until browned and nearly cooked through.

instructions.name: Add vegetables
instructions.text: Add bell pepper and onion and stir-fry 3 minutes.

instructions.name: Sauce
instructions.text: Whisk orange juice, zest, soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, ginger, and garlic. Pour into the pan and simmer 2 minutes.

instructions.name: Thicken and serve
instructions.text: Stir in the cornstarch slurry until glossy. Serve over rice with scallions and sesame seeds.

why_it_works: Fresh orange juice gives acidity and aroma that bottled sauces often lack.
A light cornstarch coat helps sauce cling to the chicken.
Vegetables cook briefly so the bowl keeps crunch.
swaps: Use honey instead of brown sugar.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet or microwave with a splash of water.
notes: Zest the orange before juicing it.
Do not add the slurry until the sauce is simmering.

faqs.q: Can I make it less sweet?
Can I use bottled orange juice?
faqs.a: Yes, but fresh juice and zest taste brighter.
No. Add crushed red pepper if you want heat.

title: Sesame-Lime Steak Crunch Salad
dek: Seared steak over crisp greens, radish, cucumber, and herbs with a punchy sesame-lime dressing.
image_alt: Steak salad with radish greens cucumber and sesame lime dressing

instructions.name: Season steak
instructions.text: Pat steak dry and season with salt and pepper.

instructions.name: Sear
instructions.text: Cook in a hot skillet with oil until browned and done to your preference. Rest 8 minutes, then slice thinly.

instructions.name: Whisk dressing
instructions.text: Combine lime juice, rice vinegar, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, ginger, and 1 tablespoon water.

instructions.name: Toss salad
instructions.text: Combine romaine, cabbage, cucumber, radish, carrot, and herbs with most of the dressing.

instructions.name: Finish
instructions.text: Top with sliced steak, nuts, and the remaining dressing.

why_it_works: Rested steak stays juicy and slices cleanly.
Two crunchy greens keep the salad substantial.
Lime, vinegar, and ginger cut through rich steak.
swaps: Add cooked rice or quinoa to make it a grain bowl.
storage: Store steak and salad separately up to 3 days. Dress only what you plan to eat.
notes: Dry greens thoroughly so the dressing clings.

faqs.a: Sirloin, flank, skirt, or strip steak all work.

faqs.q: Can I make the dressing ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Refrigerate up to 5 days and shake well before using.

title: Hot Honey Chicken with Sweet Potatoes & Asparagus
dek: Roasted chicken thighs, caramelized sweet potatoes, and asparagus finished with tangy hot-honey mustard.
image_alt: Roasted chicken with sweet potatoes and asparagus
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb sweet potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch cubes

instructions.name: Start the potatoes
instructions.text: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil, paprika, garlic powder, and half the salt. Roast 15 minutes.

instructions.name: Add chicken
instructions.text: Season chicken with remaining salt and 1/2 tablespoon oil. Add to the pan and roast 12 minutes.

instructions.name: Add asparagus
instructions.text: Toss asparagus with remaining oil and add to the pan. Roast 8 to 10 minutes more until chicken reaches 165°F.

instructions.name: Mix hot honey
instructions.text: Whisk honey, Dijon, vinegar, hot sauce, and melted butter.

instructions.name: Finish
instructions.text: Brush chicken with hot honey and drizzle a little over the vegetables. Broil 1 to 2 minutes for caramelized edges if desired.

why_it_works: Sweet potatoes get a head start so everything finishes together.
Mustard and vinegar keep hot honey from tasting one-note.
Broiling at the end creates restaurant-style lacquered edges.
swaps: Use chicken breasts cut into thick strips.
Swap asparagus for broccoli or green beans.
Use maple syrup instead of honey.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat on a sheet pan or in an air fryer.
notes: Cut sweet potatoes evenly for predictable timing.
Watch closely under the broiler because honey burns quickly.

faqs.a: With 1 teaspoon hot sauce it is mild. Increase to taste.
Yes. It reheats especially well in an air fryer.
Yes, but start it with the potatoes and allow additional cook time.
